$schema-note: Mutation LEDGER for the remaining two channel runtimes. Every row was APPLIED to the named file in the working tree, the named command was run from the repository root, the file was restored, and the recorded exit code is what that run returned. `killedCases` are read back out of the command's own output. Nothing here is a prediction.
tranche: M4.5 — packages/adapters/channel-whatsapp and packages/adapters/channel-telegram (founder decision D10)
procedure: node scripts/run-win271-mutations.mjs scripts/win271-channels-rest-mutation-plan.json scripts/mutations-win271-channels-rest.json — the same committed driver as the Slack and Discord sweeps, with two new command groups. Adapter rows run the adapters' vitest suites; wiring rows run core-api's config or installation suites.
history: THE FIRST RUN OF THIS SWEEP WAS VACUOUS AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN DISCARDED. It reported 49/49 killed, and every adapter row was a FALSE KILL: `scripts/arch/clean-v1.test.mjs` runs `pnpm build:v1` and then `pnpm clean:v1` against the REAL repository root, so it had deleted `packages/contexts/channels/dist` earlier in the session. Every adapter vitest run then failed to resolve `@platos/context-channels/application/ports/index.js` and exited 1 whatever the mutation was. It was caught because a hand re-run of one row printed a module-resolution error instead of a failing case name, and because the driver's `killedCases` were EMPTY for rows that should have named one. The sweep was re-run after `pnpm build:v1`; every figure below is from that run. A warm tree lies in both directions.

THE SECOND RUN (49 rows) killed 43 and left SIX survivors, each of which found a real gap rather than a defect in the code: W14 judged the never-connected list against `ECONNRESET`, a code `fetch` never produces here; W23's rule (the WhatsApp verify token is required with the app secret) was guarded by no case at all; T01 left the length guard in place so removing the digest changed nothing; T19 added an argument TypeScript ignores at run time; T20's edit case used a PRIVATE chat, which has no topic to leak; and T22's length case read the same constant the mutation widened. FOUR CASES WERE WRITTEN AND TWO ROWS RE-AIMED in response: the code a real dropped socket produces is now read off the wire and fed to the classifier (both adapters), the WhatsApp group's required pair and the Telegram token's alphabet and floor are proven in `apps/core-api/src/config/platform.test.ts`, an edit INSIDE a topic is proven to carry no `message_thread_id`, and both vendors' documented 4096-character limits are pinned as transcriptions so a behavioural case cannot be widened with the constant it reads.

THE THIRD RUN (52 rows) killed 50. The two survivors are DELIBERATE and are kept as recorded equivalent mutants, each with its reason in the row's `guards`: W14b (ECONNRESET's membership is unobservable on this runtime) and T01b (with the length guard in place the digest is functionally invisible; what it buys is a comparison that is constant-time in the token's LENGTH, which no behavioural case can see, and it is kept rather than deleted because that property is real).

mutations.name: T01b the digest is removed but the length guard stays
mutations.guards: nothing a functional case can observe — RECORDED AS AN EQUIVALENT MUTANT. With the guard in place a length mismatch is still FALSE and still not a throw. What the digest buys is that the comparison is constant-time in the token's LENGTH as well as its bytes: without it the guard returns early for a wrong-length token and an attacker learns the length by timing. No behavioural case can see that, and the digest is kept rather than deleted because the property is real.
